solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Shrewd, taking the beginning of the month off

indicators.note: with 'off', these words tell us to strip away the opening letter of the month named
completes the instruction: the starting letter is taken off the word

parts.note: March is a month of the year

explanation.surface: Someone canny takes the first day of the month as holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking the beginning of ... off' drops the M from MARCH; 'the beginning of the month' reads like a date but is the letter M.
explanation.definitionFit: Arch can mean knowing or cunning, as in an arch smile, a sense close to shrewd.

clue.text: Inherited ruins of Lancaster

indicators.note: a ruined thing is broken apart, so the letters of the city name are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone has inherited the crumbling remains of Lancaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruins of' signals rearranging the nine letters of LANCASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ancestral is passed down from forebears, i.e. inherited.

clue.text: Polish university officer covered in salt

indicators.note: the university and officer are wrapped inside the word for salt, which covers them

parts.note: to salt meat is to cure it
Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant, an officer

explanation.surface: A university officer is caked in salt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' as a noun means refinement, not the nationality or shoe shine.
explanation.definitionFit: Culture as refinement of taste and manners is a synonym of polish in its noun sense.

clue.text: Work found in sea transport

indicators.note: the word for work is located inside the sea, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: the Med is short for the Mediterranean Sea
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A job turns up in shipping by sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A moped is a small motorised bike, a means of transport.

clue.text: Act as time runs out for champ

indicators.note: running out suggests things scattering, so the letters of the three words are mixed up

explanation.surface: A boxing champion has to act before the clock runs down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'champ' looks like a champion but is the verb to chew noisily.
explanation.definitionFit: To champ is to chew vigorously, and masticate is the formal word for chewing.

clue.text: Cues for pint during seaside walks

indicators.note: the pint occurs in the middle of the walks, so it goes inside

parts.note: proms are promenades along a seafront

explanation.surface: Someone is prompted to stop for a pint on a stroll along the front.
explanation.walkthrough: PROM is short for promenade, a British seaside walkway.
explanation.definitionFit: Prompts are reminders or signals to act, the same as cues given to actors.

clue.text: Takes a risk on chops

definitions.meaning: to dice, as in dice with death, is to gamble or take chances
to dice food is to chop it into small cubes

explanation.surface: Someone gambles on cutting things up.
explanation.definitionFit: Dice serves both as a verb for gambling dangerously and for cutting into cubes.

clue.text: Fish sauce — at last there's a set of rules

parts.note: cod is a fish

indicators.note: signals the final letter of the word sauce

explanation.surface: A fish dish with sauce, followed by a book of regulations.
explanation.definitionFit: A code, such as a highway code, is a body of rules.

clue.text: Eggs on reserve in handy container

parts.note: a clutch is a set of eggs laid together
to bag something is to reserve or claim it

explanation.surface: Eggs kept in reserve in a convenient box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'handy' means held in the hand: a clutch bag has no strap.
explanation.definitionFit: A clutch bag is a small strapless handbag, carried in the hand, hence handy.

clue.text: Merit low exam grades — start playing tennis!

parts.note: D and E are low marks on an exam
a tennis point begins with a serve

explanation.surface: Poor marks deserve a break on the tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: To merit something is to be worthy of it, the meaning of deserve.

clue.text: Crash studies lead to inevitable conflict

parts.note: a crash is a collision
a course is a programme of studies

explanation.surface: Studying car crashes leads to unavoidable clashes.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on a collision course means heading for an unavoidable clash, a path that leads to conflict.

clue.text: Look lost if shut

indicators.note: lost implies scattered or out of place, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone looks lost when the door is shut.
explanation.walkthrough: SHUFTI is British slang, from army use, for a quick look.
explanation.definitionFit: A shufti is informal British slang for a glance or quick inspection.

clue.text: Where to write for job requiring wit

parts.note: a post is a job or position
a card is a witty, amusing person

explanation.surface: Applying for a job that needs a sense of humour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'card' is an old-fashioned word for a joker.
explanation.definitionFit: A postcard is something you write on, a place to put a message.

clue.text: Soldiers capture unknown informer and producer of grain

indicators.note: the soldiers enclose the unknown, holding it inside

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, British army soldiers
y is an algebraic unknown
a grass is British slang for a police informer

explanation.surface: Troops seize a mystery informant who supplies cereal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ryegrass is a cereal-type grass whose plants bear seed, so it is a producer of grain.

clue.text: Government gives approval and provides satisfaction

parts.note: to ratify is to give formal approval

explanation.surface: Official sign-off from the state pleases everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Gratifies means pleases, i.e. provides satisfaction.

clue.text: Fit to be included in Civil Service, having strong links

indicators.note: the word for fit goes inside the abbreviation

parts.note: able means fit or capable

explanation.surface: A capable person joins the civil service and has good connections.
explanation.definitionFit: Cables are thick ropes or wires, strong links between things.

clue.text: Softened and served dish on cue

indicators.note: served suggests something dished up in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dish is softened before being served on cue.
explanation.definitionFit: Cushioned means softened, as a blow is cushioned by padding.

clue.text: Avoids backing favourites in teams

indicators.note: the turned word sits inside the teams

parts.note: sides are teams

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the word for favourites is read backwards

parts.note: pets are favourites, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: Avoiding backing the favourite teams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns PETS into STEP, which goes inside SIDES.
explanation.definitionFit: To sidestep a problem is to avoid it.

clue.text: Access given to the French ambassador

parts.note: le is French for the
a gate gives access

explanation.surface: Entry granted to the French envoy.
explanation.definitionFit: A legate is an envoy, especially of the Pope, so an ambassador.

clue.text: Point to understand about cover for fugitive

parts.note: E, east, is a compass point

indicators.note: the word for understand goes around the cover

parts.note: to see is to understand
a cap is a covering, as a lid or hat

explanation.surface: Someone makes a point of understanding the need to hide a runaway.
explanation.definitionFit: An escapee is someone who has escaped, i.e. a fugitive.

clue.text: Left, but became reconciled

definitions.meaning: ... as in accepted, ... to one's fate

explanation.surface: Someone quit but came to terms with it.
explanation.definitionFit: Resigned means both quit a post and came to accept something unwelcome.

clue.text: Organism that's disturbingly rife under rubbish

indicators.note: in a down answer, the anagram goes below the word for rubbish

parts.note: rot means rubbish or nonsense

indicators.note: disturbing things moves them around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A creature thriving disturbingly in a heap of rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotifer is a microscopic aquatic animal, a tiny organism.

clue.text: Making enquiries about hospital and taking in food

indicators.note: the enquiries word wraps around the hospital letter

parts.note: nosing is poking about, prying

explanation.surface: Asking questions around the hospital while eating.
explanation.walkthrough: NOSH is British slang for food.
explanation.definitionFit: Noshing is informal for eating, taking in food.

clue.text: One day spent in stress as a consequence of 8

indicators.note: the one and the day are spent inside the stress, so they go within

parts.note: an accent is a stress on a syllable
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A day spent stressed as a result of a crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 refers to 8 across, a collision course; an accident follows.
explanation.definitionFit: An accident can result from heading for a collision.

clue.text: Be first to support old lover

indicators.note: in a down answer the second piece sits below the first, holding it up

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
1st, written IST, is first

explanation.surface: Be the first to stand by a former partner.
explanation.definitionFit: To exist is simply to be.

clue.text: One gets up and blooms

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
rises means gets up

explanation.surface: One person rises as the flowers open.
explanation.definitionFit: Irises are flowers, so blooms.

clue.text: Construction to really care about?

parts.note: a grammatical construction in which an adverb such as really sits between to and its verb

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase to really care is the textbook example of this grammatical construction.

clue.text: Understands energy absorbed by fast cars

indicators.note: the energy is taken in by the cars, going inside

parts.note: GTs are grand tourers, fast cars
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: He grasps that energy is soaked up by sports cars.
explanation.definitionFit: To get something is to understand it.

clue.text: Made an effort to promote one, being exhausted

indicators.note: promoting moves the one higher in the word, earlier in an across entry

parts.note: tried means made an effort
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone tried to get a colleague promoted and is worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to promote one' shifts I forward in TRIED.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone worn out or drained of energy is described as weary.

clue.text: A long time to get salary topped

indicators.note: topped means the head is cut off, removing the first letter

parts.note: wages are pay, a salary

explanation.surface: It takes ages for pay to be raised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topped' looks like increased but means beheaded.
explanation.definitionFit: Ages means a very long time.
